talks.title: Day 1 Keynote: David "DWIZZZLE" Weston: AI at the Edge: Attacks and Defense
talks.teaser: Security researchers examine technical aspects of Day 1 Keynote: David "DWIZZZLE" Weston: AI at the Edge: Attacks and Defense.
talks.summary:
Overview: David "DWIZZZLE" Weston delivers the BlueHat India Day 1 keynote on AI at the edge, covering Windows integration with neural processing units and on-device AI security implications.

Key Topics: AI and Windows security convergence; neural processing units (NPUs) for efficient on-device inference; tensor processing on specialized ASICs; and security implications of edge AI deployment.

Technical Details: Weston explains how NPUs enable 50+ teraflops of AI compute without battery impact, using matrix operations on tensors. He discusses Windows and Surface integration of AI capabilities across the device ecosystem.

Takeaways: Edge AI deployment via NPUs changes the security landscape for Windows devices. Both offensive and defensive practitioners must understand on-device AI capabilities and their attack surfaces.

talks.title: Goodbye HTA, Hello MSI: Unveiling New TTPs and Clusters of an APT...
talks.teaser: Engineers explore architecture and security mechanisms for Goodbye HTA, Hello MSI: Unveiling New TTPs and Clusters of an APT....
talks.summary:
SideCopy APT Overview

Satwick, a senior researcher on Zscaler's APT team, profiles SideCopy—a South Asian nation-state group linked to Transparent Tribe. Active since 2019, it initially mirrored Sidewinder TTPs using HTA stagers and DLL sideloading to deploy open-source RATs like Allakore.

Tactical Evolution

The group progressed from Indian defense targeting and WinRAR zero-day abuse to power-sector campaigns in India and Afghanistan with custom payloads (ReverseRAT, NightFury). By 2023–2024 it operated multiplatform clusters simultaneously attacking Windows and Linux with in-house RATs, shifting primary staging from HTA toward MSI-based delivery.

Infrastructure and Overlap

Researchers map infection chains across clusters—MSHTA in-memory DLL execution on Windows paralleled by Golang ELF binaries establishing cron persistence on Linux. Shared C2 infrastructure and decoys show correlations with APT36, including education-portal compromises hosting both groups' payloads.

2024–2025 Targeting and Response

Recent campaigns use honey-trap and government-themed lures against officials and university students. Satwick closes with detection and hunting guidance, emphasizing that SideCopy weaponizes trust and free tooling against both national-security and civilian victims.

talks.title: Variant Hunting: How MSRC Uses Submission Data to Find Security Vulnerabilities
talks.teaser: Analysts investigate attack surfaces and defenses concerning Variant Hunting: How MSRC Uses Submission Data to Find Security Vulnerabilities.
talks.summary:
Why competitions matter to MSRC

The speaker focuses MSRC variant hunting on Tianfu Cup and Pwn2Own submissions against real platforms like Windows, unlike CTF-style intentionally vulnerable apps. Competitions incentivize reliable, novel exploits with limited demo attempts, driving deep research MSRC wants to prevent.

Research snowball effect

Public writeups and proof-of-concept releases after competitions attract follow-on research. A kernel streaming example shows a small 2023 Pwn2Own blip followed by roughly 50 MSRC cases, active exploitation, and another competition submission months later.

MSRC's response process

After major events, MSRC produces detailed post-competition reports with root-cause and exploit analysis to inform system-class mitigations beyond single bugs. The team variant-hunts every competition submission, searching for related vulnerabilities. Tianfu Cup 2023 had two Windows EoP bugs; Pwn2Own 2024 brought nine submissions, six against Windows.

talks.title: Serverless Phishing 2.0: Cloud Workers in Identity based Attacks
talks.teaser: Analysts investigate attack surfaces and defenses concerning Serverless Phishing 2.0: Cloud Workers in Identity based Attacks.
talks.summary:
MFA is not enough

Presenters Yash and Manish open by noting strong passwords and MFA do not stop modern phishing. Attackers host convincing login pages on trusted cloud domains—AWS, Azure, GCP, Cloudflare Workers—evading reputation filters until victims already submit credentials and tokens.

Token theft over passwords

The talk details OAuth access tokens, refresh tokens that silently renew sessions, and SSO tokens that grant broad application access without repeating full login flows. Capturing these artifacts gives prolonged unauthorized access even when password policies are sound.

Targeting identity platforms

Adversaries now prioritize identity provider and admin portals (Microsoft 365, AWS console, EDR management) over endpoint malware because EDR/XDR makes traditional persistence harder. Serverless and cloud-worker hosting lowers attacker infrastructure cost while blending into allow-listed domains defenders trust.

talks.title: Agentic AI: Simulating Autonomous Adversaries with AI-Driven Red Teaming
talks.teaser: Presenters detail vulnerability discovery and exploitation in Agentic AI: Simulating Autonomous Adversaries with AI-Driven Red Teaming.
talks.summary:
## Overview
In this presentation, threat hunter Shreya from Microsoft examines the evolution of offensive security and introduces agentic AI as the next paradigm shift in red teaming simulations. Unlike legacy script- or playbook-driven automated attacks, agentic AI operates with an autonomous reasoning engine and memory, allowing it to adapt mid-run rather than merely post-failure. The research centers on bridging frameworks like MITRE ATLAS and MITRE ATT&CK with adaptive reasoning models, aiming to simulate an adversary’s tactical intent alongside specific execution techniques.

## Evolution of Adversary Tactics
The speaker outlines the historical progression of threat actors leading up to autonomous AI:
- **Handcrafted Payloads:** Early attackers who functioned as artisans manually crafting exploits.
- **Script Kiddies:** Attackers armed with automated tools but lacking deep tactical understanding.
- **Sophisticated Malware Kits & Professionalized APTs:** Persistent adversaries operating with advanced kits, though still bound to static playbooks.
- **Agentic AI:** Autonomous entities capable of understanding defense contexts, learning mid-execution, and rewriting attack paths dynamically. Industry context underscores this shift, citing a Gartner brief projecting that agentic AI will handle 80% of customer support interactions by 2029, as well as Microsoft and Nvidia identifying agentic AI as a major technological frontier.

## Agentic AI Architecture and Components
The functional architecture of the red teaming agent is structured around specialized modular roles collaborating as a mission control team:
- **Scout ("Sam"):** Gathers external and internal intelligence, such as scanning for DNS leaks, harvesting credentials from the dark web, or pulling telemetry logs.
- **LLM-Driven Analyst:** Ingests intelligence gathered by the scout, compares observed conditions to historical attack data, and reasons through the operational picture.
- **Planner ("Mission Brain"):** Establishes objectives and charts end-to-end attack paths spanning initial access, lateral movement, and data exfiltration.
- **Executor:** Directly performs tactical actions autonomously without human intervention, including phishing campaigns, proxy rotation, and living-off-the-land binary (LOLBin) execution.
- **Fallback / Learning Loop:** Incorporates a continuous feedback loop powered by a vector database. It registers successful and failed actions to ensure subsequent outputs become faster and more evasive.
- **Model / Persona Layer:** Configures the agent's behavioral profiles to mirror specific Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs).

## Methodologies and Ongoing Research
The session highlights practical applications and ongoing research initiatives:
- **Real-World Attack Simulations:** Scenarios evaluated include adaptive EDR evasion and credential stuffing attacks (referencing real-world paradigms like the 2020 Spotify credential stuffing incident).
- **Framework Integration:** Mapping adaptive reasoning directly against MITRE ATT&CK (enterprise techniques) and MITRE ATLAS (adversarial threat landscape for artificial intelligence systems).
- **Project Aether:** A research model developed by the speaker designed to simulate not merely discrete attacker techniques, but genuine adversary intent and continuous adaptation against active defensive measures.
